answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy makes trust expensive to fake: every new identity starts with zero reputation and must complete a verifiable voyage of small, attested tasks before it can transact at scale. Like a falcon proven by its hunts rather than its plumage, an agent's credential is its signed history of graded deliveries, recorded in an umber ledger that anyone can audit. Spinning up thousands of fresh identities gains nothing, because each one must still earn its way in, one verified task at a time.
